blocks.text: Routes listed and routes drawn

How many routes each country's or region's own register lists, how many of them the atlas draws, and why each of the rest is absent. A route counts once in each state or province it runs through, because that is how every register is kept: FHWA lists I-95 once in each of its fifteen states. "Drawn" means the atlas has a route of that number there. Where it is drawn under a different number, the reason says so and it counts as absent, except for Mexico's state roads, whose numbering D-26 leaves to INEGI.

Written by `tools/coverage-figures.mjs` from the build, the two cross-checks (`npm run check:us`, `npm run check:mx`) and the reasons established by hand in `content/reference/coverage-gaps.json`. `npm test` rewrites it, and fails on an absence that has no reason.
Each decision states what was decided, why, and what was rejected. **Enforced** names the code that holds the rule, so changing the decision means changing that code.
Rules for every source

head: ID
Decision
Why, and what was rejected
Enforced
rows: Every figure is measured, reported or published, and the three are never mixed or used to fill in for one another.
A blend cannot be checked against either source.
Reported figures are joined to a route by designation, never by position.
A spatial join lets a wrong geometry quietly acquire the right count.
A figure covering part of a road states the share it covers.
A measure over a fifth of a road, shown as the road's, is a fabrication.
the `cover` field on every HPMS and provincial measure
Where a source says nothing, the site says nothing: no zero, no estimate.
A zero reads as a measurement.
A route's length is measured once, along the path you would drive.
Summing every centreline counted Highway 401 at 1,819 km against 828.
A published figure carries a source, or a reason none exists, in English and Chinese.
A dossier names its road by system, number and, where the number repeats, an anchor point; never by the id a build assigned.
Build ids moved when US geometry changed source, and 26 dossiers silently stopped showing.
A dossier's "no public figure" for a route's cost is dropped where FHWA's route cost table has one, and reported.
The page otherwise printed both side by side.
The README's figures are written from the build.
Typed figures drifted from the data they described.
An absent edition or licence is recorded as `null` or "none stated", never guessed.
A guessed edition makes a re-fetch look like a correction.
A ring road whose farthest point is the tip of a stub is closed from the nodes within 5 km of either end of its path.
The stub has no way back, so Kansas City's I-435 measured 33 mi in Missouri and filed its Kansas half as branches; it now measures 81 mi against FHWA's 80.74. Only I-435 changed.

A piece under half a mile beside a longer piece of the same number is dropped; a short road that is the only one of its number is kept and shown as "<1 mi". The stitcher's sliver threshold (1.2 km US, 1.5 km Canada and Mexico) likewise applies only where the number has a longer piece. An American state number whose only piece is under half a mile is still left out, as it was under the threshold.

The ten dropped were digitising remnants listed as routes of 0 mi. Their siblings lost the `-1` suffix they needed only to tell the two apart (`us-129-ga-1` is now `us-129`). The threshold had also discarded whole roads shorter than it: Ontario's 7000-series links, Manitoba 29 to the border at Emerson. In the United States it would have added some 1,200 routes of under half a mile, nearly all a few hundred metres of a farm-to-market or secondary road that TIGER classes higher at an interchange, the rest of which D-47 leaves out.

`build-data.mjs` removes per-jurisdiction geometry files it no longer writes, and `check-data.mjs`, run by `npm test`, fails on any disagreement between the index, the geometry files and every file that names a route.
A stale `DC.json` outlived the DC 295 that TIGER 2025 now files as I-295, and an id change in one build silently empties another file's references.

Where only one of a route's two carriageways is kept, each duplicate piece is filed with the kept piece it runs beside most, not with the first. The ends chosen as the pair farthest apart on the map are then moved on along the road wherever it continues past them to a dead end, unless the way there crosses a bridged gap or the new end lies within 2 km, or an eighth of the added length, of the road already walked.

The first rule had filed Florida's I-295 ring under New Jersey's I-295. The ends are found across the map, so a road that hooks back had its far end mid-hook: I-295 runs north up New Jersey to Bordentown and then west through Lawrence into Pennsylvania, and Bordentown was taken for the end, with the last 30 mi, FHWA's 10.82 in Pennsylvania among them, filed as a branch. It now measures 93 mi against 93.08. Some 320 routes gained length, none lost any, and the Interstates among them moved toward the Route Log (I-275 FL 51 to 59 against 60.3, I-215 UT 26 to 28 against 29); others reach their published lengths, as M-22 at 116 mi, HI-11 at 122, Arizona's Loop 202 at 77, WA-503 at 54. I-287 now begins at Edison rather than Green Knoll, 98 mi. Without the margin the far carriageway is walked back to the start: I-17 measured Tempe to Tempe.
Every list, ranking and total gives a route's measured length. An official length appears only in the route's panel, beside the measurement and with its source.

The route index had carried FHWA's figure where one existed and the measurement otherwise, so 190 Interstates were ranked by a different kind of number from their neighbours (I-90 at 2,706 against 3,076 measured), against D-1.

A dossier's official length is for the stretch the atlas draws. Where the Route Log has a figure for the route, the dossier may not give another; otherwise its figure lies within 20% of the measurement, or `officialCovers` names the atlas routes it spans and the page compares it with their measured sum. The build fails on either. Where the Route Log omits a jurisdiction the route crosses for under 2 mi, the per-state join is no longer blocked by it.

Dossiers had cited a part as the whole: I-49 249.93 mi, Louisiana alone, against 559 measured; I-69 523.36 for two of its three states; I-75 and I-81 the Tennessee figures D-53 corrects; I-295 a figure for a different extent. AK-3's 323 and TX 71's 253 span two and three of the atlas's pieces. The Route Log could not be joined to I-49 at all, because it runs 1 mi into Texas, where the log lists no I-49.

head: ID
Decision
Why, and what was rejected
Enforced
rows: Reproducible builds; the Census keeps past years.
Designations are parsed from the road name; historic alignments (`Old US Hwy 395`, `Hst Rte 66`) are excluded; concurrencies (`US Hwy 11/15`) count for both routes.
HPMS is queried and summed server-side, one row per route per state, rather than downloaded.
The release is 19.5 million sections and 49 GB.
HPMS figures for a multi-state route are weighted by the miles measured in each state.
A flat average lets New Hampshire's 15 miles of I-95 count as much as Florida's 382.
Texas, Massachusetts and Maryland are matched on HPMS `route_id`; Tennessee is left unmatched.
Those states do not report `route_signing` usably; no reliable key exists for Tennessee.
Alaska's A-1 to A-4 are declared as the state routes they overlay plus two termini.
They carry no Interstate shields, so no geometry names them.
Construction cost is FHWA's 1991 estimate: Interstate Construction funds only, obligations to 31 December 1989, not inflation-adjusted.
It is the only route-by-route federal figure; turnpikes built without IC funds are absent from it.
The buildout map lights only routes with a documented opening year; the curve is FHWA's national series.

The American network is TIGER's primary and secondary roads (MTFCC S1100 and S1200), every signed route on them included. State routes TIGER files only among local roads are out of scope: North Carolina's secondary routes, South Carolina's S-roads, most Texas farm-to-market roads.

HPMS lists some 11,000 state route numbers the atlas lacks, nearly all of them these local-grade systems. Reading TIGER's full road files to add them was rejected: they are the size of every street in the country, and a farm road is not what the atlas maps.

A name that is itself a designation is read as one although TIGER types it `M`: in Puerto Rico a name beginning "PR" or "Carr", anywhere a name beginning "I-", and in Texas a loop or spur, including those filed without the word "State" (Tyler's Loop 49, San Angelo's Loop 250). TIGER's tables are read as UTF-8.

Elsewhere `M` marks a common name and is refused, but TIGER types every Puerto Rican carretera `M`, PR-52 included, so the whole island was missing, as were Laredo's "I-69 W" and the two Texas loops. Read as Windows-1252, "Peña Blvd" came out as "PeÃ±a".

A TIGER primary road with a name and no number becomes part of a route where no numbered route runs within 0.4 km of it. Where FHWA's Route Log shows the named road is a signed route, it joins that route (the Natcher Parkway is I-165); otherwise it is a route of its own, titled by its name, with an empty shield and a note that it has no number, if it measures a mile or more; a shorter one stays a context line. Unsigned internal numbers (Kentucky's 9000-series, New Jersey's 444 and 700, Oklahoma's turnpike numbers) are not shown.

S1100 is TIGER's limited-access class, so these were freeways drawn only as context hairlines: the Kentucky parkways, the John Kilpatrick Turnpike, Puerto Rico's expressways. The shorter ones are interchanges on ordinary arterials (Jamboree Road, Cedar Avenue), not freeways. No source the atlas reads carries the internal numbers: HPMS has no Kentucky 900x or New Jersey 444/700 rows, and its Oklahoma 375 is 209 mi, a different extent.

Route Log figures shown to be misfiled are replaced from `fhwa-corrections.json`, each with the figure FHWA publishes; the build fails if a published figure changes. A figure with no recoverable value is withdrawn, which leaves its route to the measurement (D-1). The first case is Tennessee, whose mileage column in both tables is shifted one row from I-69 to I-840.

The shifted values fit route by route: I-640 was published at 77.29 mi (I-840's length) against 11 measured, I-81 at 1.96 (I-124's) against 76, I-75 at 75.63 (I-81's) against 159, which is 142.23 plus its 19.60 mi on I-40. Dropping only the implausible rows was rejected, as it would have left the plausible-looking wrong ones.

TIGER segments that carry the wrong name are read under the right one from `tiger-renames.json`, each entry listing its segments by LINEARID and giving its reason; the build fails if TIGER's year changes or an entry no longer matches. A line TIGER draws out and back along one road is split at its far end, where 80% of the way back lies within 100 m of the way out. A corridor's breaks are also bridged from each piece's extremities (D-56), since I-35 now stops at the Twin Cities split where its carriageways meet.

Plain "I- 35" between the Twin Cities split and rejoin is I-35E or I-35W, segment by segment; the M-typed "Joe N Martin Expy" is I-555; Indiana's State Road 265 has been I-265 since 2019; I-11 has run on US 95 from Railroad Pass to Kyle Canyon since 2024, and I-515, decommissioned and not in the Route Log, is dropped. A folded line had left I-73 at 70 mi with the rest drawn as a branch. Matching by name alone was rejected, since "I- 35" is also the through route on either side of the split. Splitting every line whose ends lie close was rejected: a loop is drawn that way too, and halving one at Fort Johnson moved NY 5's end from Albany to Tribes Hill.

blocks.text: Canada

head: ID
Decision
Why, and what was rejected
Enforced
rows: Municipal and county numbers in the NRN are kept, the tier is named "Provincial & Municipal", and each road is told apart by place.
The file does not distinguish them; guessing would drop real provincial highways.
`RTNUMBER` 0 means no number; decimals (`1.0`) are trimmed; Newfoundland's local-access numbers (`430-15`) are excluded.
Each produced false routes: a 42,465 km "Highway 0", 2,504 false NL routes.
Replaced by D-52. The Trans-Canada tier was measured from the NRN's segment names: a route carrying it for at least 25 km and 35% of its length.

The names are missing from British Columbia's Yellowhead and from all of Quebec, so both were drawn as ordinary routes, and a route that qualified was drawn as Trans-Canada end to end: all of Highway 400 and Highway 11.

The Trans-Canada is the routes on a hand-kept list (`tch-routes.json`): the main route and every branch Wikipedia lists, 33 routes in ten provinces. Each is split where the designation ends, so only the stretch that carries it is drawn as Trans-Canada and the rest stays in its own tier. The extent is the NRN's own segment names wherever the province records them, and otherwise the whole route (BC 1, whose Island stretch the NRN leaves unnamed, BC 16, QC 85, QC 185) or the stretch between two junctions (ON 11, so that a stray named piece west of Highway 71 is not drawn, and QC 40, 25, 20, 117 and 15). NRN names on routes not on the list are pavement shared with a listed route, and are ignored; `tch-crosscheck.json` lists both. Ferry crossings are not drawn.

No machine-readable register of the system exists, so it is a small closed set assembled by hand under [§2](#2-what-a-source-must-meet); Transport Canada's backgrounder confirms the main route and the Yellowhead but lists no branches, which is why the encyclopedia is used to enumerate them, against the authority rule. Measuring the tier from names alone (D-21) was rejected for the gaps it left.

In Ontario, outside its Trans-Canada stretches, a number's pieces are joined only across breaks of up to 15 km. Pieces farther apart are separate routes under the same number, told apart by the place at their end; their ids are numbered by length, so `on-12-on-1` is a Huron county road and the provincial highway is `on-12-on-3`.

Ontario files county roads under the numbers of its provincial highways, so the NHS stitching (up to 120 km per break) welded Highway 12's Whitby–Midland corridor to county roads 12 across the province, and gave its far end as the Town of Essex, 350 km away. Its provincial stretches break only at connecting links through towns, which 15 km spans. Telling a provincial stretch from a county road by road class was rejected, since a connecting link is classed as an arterial like the county roads.
NHS designation is read from Transport Canada's service.
StatCan's own NHS layers are empty for NT and YT.
Traffic is read only from jurisdictions that publish in bulk; each figure is a length-weighted average shown beside the busiest point.
Maps and PDFs fail [§2](#2-what-a-source-must-meet); an average alone hides the peak.
Ontario's shared-pavement crediting is kept as published; Nova Scotia's one-direction counts are summed into a two-way figure; Highway 407's operator trips are not shown as traffic.
Each is stated on the route panel.
Opening years come only from Quebec's répertoire and the dated Year Book events.
No other province publishes them; bridge years are refused (D-36).

A provincial route the NRN gives no number is left out, not added from another source. Known cases: Alberta 12A and 834A; Nova Scotia 32, 33, 253, 280, 318, 322 and 328; New Brunswick 151, 189, 194, 195 and 197; ten Ontario 7000-series links (7087 to 7908) and 7187; Saskatchewan 10A, Yukon 97 and Quebec 720 from the NHS register. Each is listed in `coverage-gaps.json`.

Provincial counts and registers name them, but only the NRN supplies Canadian geometry with a licence that meets [§2](#2-what-a-source-must-meet); a provincial count file's sections cannot supply a road the national file lacks.

head: ID
Decision
Why, and what was rejected
Enforced
rows: Route numbers follow INEGI's CODIGO; SICT's numbering is cross-checked, not merged.
The two agencies number state roads independently; merging would invent routes.
Only numbered roads become routes; unnumbered federal and state roads of 2 km or more are faint background.
An unnumbered road has no designation to join anything to.
MEX-15 and MEX-15D are one route; toll share comes from the per-segment flag.
The file almost never writes the D suffix.
A federal segment's state is found against Natural Earth 1:10m.
The file names the federation as the jurisdiction of every federal segment.
Route ends are the SICT section (tramo) they lie on.
There is no gazetteer in the Mexican pipeline.
`VELOCIDAD` is kept as `routingSpeed` and never shown as a speed limit.
It is a routing parameter, not a posted limit.

TDPA is shown per route as the count of stations and their median, lowest and highest; no length-weighted average. Stations on unnumbered roads or more than 5 km from their route are not placed. The 2,206 sites SICT inferred for 2024 are noted, since the data does not flag them.
Stations are points; weighting them by length invents coverage.

Where SICT's latest edition holds under half a state's previous-year rows, that state's stations are the previous year's from the twelve-year panel. Each station carries its year, and a route whose stations span both shows "2023–2024". A station keyed `MEX-015D` is placed on MEX-015, as D-28 makes the two one route.

The 2024 edition stops at 99 rows in twelve states, in both resources (Jalisco 99 against 734 in 2023), a cut-off rather than a smaller survey. Using 2023 everywhere was rejected as discarding the complete 2024 states. Without the D fold, more than 2,000 stations on the toll motorways were dropped.

A state route named only as a ramal, acceso or offset is kept where SICT's 2025 index lists the same number, in the same state, for a tramo of the same name. SICT state numbers the RNC does not carry are not placed.

Refusing every such route (D-27's reasoning, `isBranchOnly`) also dropped roads two agencies designate alike: Hidalgo's HGO-017 Tepeji del Río–Tlahuelilpan, Quintana Roo's QR-018. Of the 122 SICT state designations absent from the atlas, most are roads the RNC numbers differently (D-26) or that cannot be found in it by name; placing those by position was rejected.
A federal route with no segment inside any state's generalised boundary is filed in the nearest state; its per-state mileage stays empty.
`mex-174` (Ciudad Juárez) and a Sonoran piece of MEX-15 were filed in "MX". Pushing their segments into the nearest state's mileage was rejected, as D-29 leaves such segments unassigned.
A Mexican route's breaks are bridged from each piece's two geographic extremities as well as from its dead ends. Federal numbers written only in a segment's name are not read.

The RNC draws divided federal highways as two one-way carriageways that meet at the end of each piece, so the piece has no dead end there, and the only bridges left ran from ramp stubs: MEX-85 jumped 117 km from Mante to Victoria past a 119 km piece of itself 3 km off either end, which was drawn as a branch and left out of the length. The pieces break where another number's CODIGO takes over a shared stretch (MEX-80 at Mante, MEX-2 at Nuevo Laredo), since the field holds one number. Reading numbers from NOMBRE was rejected: of 1,100 km of segments whose name writes a federal number, almost all are state roads named for the junction they leave from ("E.C. México 15 – Ocoroni"), and the few that are the highway itself are city streets.

A Taiwanese or Hong Kong route ends at the road the end lies on, as the source names it. The Highway Bureau's termini and districts are quoted beside, not matched to an end.
Neither file carries a gazetteer. The register writes 臺北—楓港 without saying which end of the drawn line is which, and placing it by position would be a join D-2 refuses.

A provincial highway's official length is the register's, against the longest piece the atlas draws of it; a national freeway has none. Hong Kong's road network records no road class, so its routes have no freeway share.

No per-route freeway length was found as open data on data.gov.tw or from the Freeway Bureau; whether to take one from another publication is open ([ACCURACY.md §6](ACCURACY.md#6-known-gaps)). Calling every Hong Kong route a freeway would be an inference.

A freeway's traffic is the Freeway Bureau's daily reference volume, shown under that name: the busiest mainline section on a weekday, the median section on a weekday, Saturday and Sunday, both directions added. The two directions of a section are paired by their unordered end names; a section without a partner is left out. Elevated carriageways are a separate row. The figures go on the longest piece of the number.

The bureau states neither the unit nor the method, so calling the figures AADT would claim what the source does not. The sections carry names, not coordinates, so the longest piece is the only placement that is not a guess. Adding the elevated 國1 to the ground road would count one corridor twice.

A provincial highway's traffic is the Highway Bureau's survey: each station's two directions added, placed on the nearest piece of its number within 5 km, and averaged over the route weighted by the length of road each station stands for, beside the busiest station, the heavy-vehicle and motorcycle shares and the share of the route the stations cover. The panel says some stations record a survey weekday or a dated closure. The Eastern office's file names its works office where a station's name belongs, so there the station is named by its section's ends.

Each station states the stretch it represents, so unlike Mexico's points (D-32) a length weighting is the source's own. In the 2025 file 442 of 1,539 rows note a weekday (四, 日, 六) and a few a dated closure in 備註, which suggests counts on given days rather than continuous ones; the bureau does not say which.

head: ID

rows: Mainland China is drawn from OpenStreetMap, the one exception to the authority rule in [§2](#2-what-a-source-must-meet). Every mainland route's panel, the length under its headline and the About page say so; the data under `data/geo/cn/` is a derived database under the ODbL.

The authority's open edition, the 1:1,000,000 public national base map, is served only through Tianditu, which answered requests from outside China with HTTP 418, and webmap.cn, which used to carry it, no longer does. No other body publishes national or provincial road geometry in bulk. Leaving the mainland out was the alternative; drawing it from OSM and saying so leaves the reader to judge. Commercial map services were rejected outright: their terms forbid extraction.

A mainland route is every way, of road class `track` and up, that carries the number on its own `ref` or through a `route=road` relation, read as GB/T 917 writes it: G with one, two or four digits, or two and a letter suffix, is a national expressway; G with three digits an ordinary national highway; S a provincial road, one route per province that uses the number. A number marked 旧, old or 原, or written G0xx (the expressway numbering the 2009 standard replaced), is left out. County (X), township (Y) and village (C) roads are not read.

The number is in the source, so nothing is matched. A provincial number is each province's own, so filing S1 across provinces as one route would join unrelated roads. County roads are numbered by each county and are far more numerous; like Ontario's county roads (D-50) they would bury the provincial tier.

A mainland way is filed in the province its middle point is in, against Natural Earth's boundaries, or the nearest within 0.2° where the generalised coastline misses it; a way in neither is outside the mainland and is left out. A route's end is named by the nearest city or town OSM maps within 30 km, a city winning over a town 8 km nearer, widening to 120 km where there is none, with the distance shown.

The extract runs over the borders, into Mongolia, Myanmar, Hong Kong and Macau. Most of the Tibetan plateau and the Taklamakan have no town within 30 km of a route's end, and an unnamed end tells the reader less than a named one with its distance.
A mainland motorway is counted as freeway whether or not it is tagged `toll=yes`, and no mainland route has a toll share.

The tag is on under a third of the expressway network: 70 of 223 expressways longer than 50 mi have it on more than half their length, on a network that is tolled almost throughout. A share read from it would measure the mapping.

A national route's name and planned ends are those of the route relation that describes the whole route (official name, then both ends, then a name with no section or direction qualifier), with section qualifiers such as （四川段） and （北京方向） stripped; the ends are quoted, not matched to the drawn line.
Mappers split a route's relation by province or by direction, and each piece repeats the route's name with its own qualifier, so picking the largest piece named G318 after its Sichuan section.

A national number's pieces are stitched across gaps of up to 30 km, then the pieces across up to 80 km; a provincial number's across 15 km. A provincial piece under 2 km is dropped where the number has a longer piece.

OSM's numbered ways break at every junction where a mapper split a way and did not carry the ref; a national route left in hundreds of pieces is not a route a reader can follow. A provincial stub at a junction is a ramp tagged with the number, not a road.

A main or ring route carries the 2022 plan's name and, where Chinese Wikipedia lists one, its length, shown as a listed length beside the drawn length and the share drawn, never as the headline. Where only a built length is listed (G3) it is labelled so. The English name is the atlas's romanisation of the planned ends, written by hand; ring routes carry no length.

The plan itself is a PDF the atlas cannot fetch, and Wikipedia's lists were the check on it already (CN-2). A planned length counts unbuilt stretches, so as a headline it would claim road that is not there. OSM's English names cover few routes and are often section names; romanising the ends keeps every main route named in English. The ring lengths listed (144 km for the Central Liaoning ring) are too short for the rings the plan describes to be trusted.

Neither register says which road a crossing is on.

A new bridge on an old road dates a replacement; roads open before their structures are finished.
A Canadian toll stretch is drawn only if it measures within 10% of the published length; a fare is shown only with the date it took effect.
A cut of a different length has found the wrong stretch; an undated fare cannot be checked.

A concession title is linked to a route only if it writes the number, or a proposed name match has `approved: true`. A grant date is shown, for a title to build, as the earliest the road could have opened. Concessions are not drawn.
Titles name roads in words; the register does not say where a concession begins or ends.

Elevation is sampled at 220 points along the mainline from zoom-9 tiles. A reading below sea level is the bed of the water a bridge, tunnel or ferry crosses, except inside the four basins where North America's dry land lies below it (the Salton Trough, Death Valley, New Orleans, the Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta); such samples take the line between the readings on either bank, never below zero.

The tiles carry bathymetry, so a crossing reads as the floor beneath it. The earlier rule, a floor at −30 m, left 22 profiles dipping as far as −96 ft over shallower water: the Sunshine Skyway, Monitor–Merrimac, the Tappan Zee, the Verrazzano, Benicia. A water mask from Natural Earth was rejected: at 1:10m it has no rivers, and the Hudson at the Tappan Zee is one.
Mexico's toll plazas are drawn as points from the RNC, with the operator, the toll system and the source's own grade of the position; only a plaza graded *definida* is shown without a note.
It is where a toll is paid, not where a tolled road begins or ends, and a closed system has one at every entry and exit, so the count is of booths.
The bridge layer draws the two inventories as published, culverts included where Ontario records them, coloured by year built, and every popup repeats D-36. The layer says which networks it covers.
The United States (NBI), Mexico's tolled network and twelve Canadian jurisdictions are absent; a layer that did not say so would read as the continent.

blocks.text: The three are never mixed, averaged, or used to fill in for one another.

Length, endpoints, per-jurisdiction mileage, straight-line span and roadway-class composition are computed here from surveyed road geometry, thinned for drawing but not redrawn. A route is measured along the single path from one end of it to the other, so a divided highway counts once rather than once per carriageway. The build compares the result with FHWA's register wherever the register has a figure, and writes the spread into `data/stats.json`; the README quotes it from there.

The larger disagreements are mostly explained rather than wrong, and the site explains them instead of splitting the difference. FHWA credits pavement shared by two Interstates to one of them, so where I-90 runs along the Indiana Toll Road with I-80 those miles are I-80's in the register and both roads' here, which is why I-90 measures 13.7% longer than published. The register also has slips of its own: its Tennessee column is shifted one row, so that Knoxville's I-640, a beltway of about seven miles, is given I-840's 77.29. Those figures are replaced from a committed correction table that keeps the published value beside each one ([D-53](DATA-SOURCES.md#5-decision-log)). Otherwise both figures are always shown, and neither is bent toward the other.
The algorithm, and the cases it cannot measure correctly, are in [ARCHITECTURE.md §3](ARCHITECTURE.md#3-from-fragments-to-routes).

Traffic volume, heavy-truck volume, pavement condition, lane counts, posted speeds and the year a road was last improved are what the states measured and reported to FHWA, joined to a route by its designation and never by position. Coverage is uneven by design: pavement condition is surveyed thoroughly on the National Highway System and patchily elsewhere, so every one of these figures states the share of the route it was measured over.

**Canada has no equivalent.** There is no national traffic collection, because counting is provincial and each province decides for itself whether to publish, in what form and under what terms. Routes in a province that does not publish carry no traffic figure rather than an inferred one.

blocks.text: Each provincial figure is an average along the route, weighted by length, shown beside the volume at the road's busiest point where the two differ. Highway 401 averages 73,700 vehicles a day along its length but carries 511,400 between Highway 427 and Renforth Drive, the highest single-point count anywhere in this atlas. Ontario's Highway 407 is the one conspicuous blank: the tolled section runs under a 99-year concession and is excluded from the ministry's counts, and the figure its operator publishes is average workday trips, which is not a daily volume and is not shown as though it were.

**Mexico counts at points.** SICT's Datos Viales gives TDPA (equivalent to AADT) at count stations on the paved national network. A route shows how many of its stations were counted and their median, lowest and highest TDPA. No length-weighted average is computed, because the stations are points, not sections, and weighting them by length would invent coverage SICT did not publish. The 2024 edition stops at 99 rows in twelve states, where 2023 had hundreds, so those states' stations are 2023's. Every route says which year it shows, and one crossing both kinds of state says "2023–2024".

Official Interstate mileage comes from the FHWA Route Log and Finder List; Canadian designations and network mileage come from Transport Canada. Everything in a written dossier (costs, traffic counts, construction dates, condition) carries its own source line naming the publication and its date. Toll facilities carry one per fact, and a fare is shown only with the date it took effect.

Where no published figure exists, the site says so rather than estimating. The Yellowhead Highway was built and extended by four provinces over decades and no department has published a total cost for it, so its page says that instead of inventing one. `build-content.mjs` enforces this: a figure must carry a source or an explanation of why it is absent, in both English and Chinese, or the build fails. Where a dossier records a cost as unpublished and FHWA's route-by-route cost table has one, the build drops the dossier's claim and reports it, so the page never prints "no public figure" beside a sourced one.

accuracy.title: What the data cannot tell apart

blocks.text: Canada's national road file records county and municipal route numbers in the same field as provincial highway numbers, with nothing to tell them apart: twenty-two separate Ontario roads carry the number 21. All are published rather than guessed at, the tier is named for it, and each road is listed with the place that identifies it.

TIGER gives each stretch of road one name. Where two routes share the pavement, the stretch carries one number and the other route has a gap there. The road is drawn, under the other number, but the route that lost the label measures short: several Interstates fall below FHWA's mileage for this reason alone. Where FHWA's figure exists, the route page shows it beside the measurement.

A grant date is not an opening date. SICT's concession register dates when a title was granted; for a title to build a road, the site shows that date as the earliest the road could have opened, and says so.
"Source" means no publisher releases it in a usable form; "pending" means it is available and not yet built.

head: Country
Gap
Kind
Detail
rows: Neither INEGI nor SICT publishes when a road opened. SICT's bridge inventory dates 9,818 federal free-network bridges; those are drawn in the bridge layer as facts about bridges, and not used to date roads.

Most states do not number their state roads. SICT's own 2025 listing gives 265 of the 711 state roads it counts a number, and only numbered roads can become routes. The state tier is the numbered minority of INEGI's 103,787 km state network.

The road file almost never writes the D suffix, so MEX-15 and MEX-15D share one number. A federal route can mix a toll and a free alignment, and parallel stretches show up as separate pieces under one number. Toll share comes from the file's per-segment toll flag.
Which state a federal road is in

The road file records the federation rather than the state as the jurisdiction of federal segments. The per-state breakdown is located against Natural Earth's 1:10m boundaries, and each route page says so.
There is no gazetteer in the Mexican pipeline, so each end is given as the SICT section (tramo) it lies on rather than as a town.
Unnumbered federal and state carreteras are drawn only as faint background, and only stretches of 2 km or more. Municipal and private carreteras are not drawn.
`VELOCIDAD` is a routing parameter, not a posted limit, and is not shown.
SICT count stations on roads with no number, or more than 5 km from their numbered route, are not placed.
State route numbers differ between agencies

INEGI and SICT number state roads independently, and the atlas follows INEGI. Of the 235 distinct state route numbers in SICT's 2025 index, 101 match an atlas route by number and name, and 55 name a road the atlas carries under a different number. Sinaloa accounts for 10 of its 18 keys (SICT's SIN-030 Culiacán–Altata is INEGI's 313), and Chihuahua for 4 of its 6. Another 27 match by number only, and 52 match nothing. Federal numbers agree: 260 of 281 state-and-number pairs are present. Per-road detail is in `content/reference/mx-crosscheck.json` (`npm run check:mx`).
SICT state routes the road file cannot place

Of the state designations in SICT's 2025 index that the atlas lacks, about half name a tramo the RNC carries under another number, and the rest name a tramo that cannot be found in the RNC by name at all (Guanajuato's GTO-001, San Luis Potosí's periférico SLP-032). They are not placed by position (D-51).
How many crossings the northern border has

Published counts disagree, and each counts something different: INDAABIN lists 45 federal border-port properties on the US border, the Instituto Mexicano del Transporte (PT 437) 52 border bridges, and the North American Development Bank's 2019 study 59 crossings after reconciling inventories, 4 of them closed. The atlas draws INDAABIN's 45 and does not prefer any of the counts. One property can hold more than one crossing, as "Nogales I y II" does.
Which road a concession is on

SICT's register of 75 federal concession titles names most roads in words, not by number. 6 titles write a route number. 35 more are linked because they write the name SICT's Datos Viales gives a road, each match proposed by `npm run propose:tolls` and accepted by hand in `content/reference/mx-concession-matches.json`. Matches on a road named only as where a concession begins or ends were rejected. The other 34 titles, mostly bridges, stay in `content/reference/mx-concessions.json`. Concessions are not drawn, since the register does not say where one begins or ends.
Neither has a Mexico view yet.
Monthly flows and historical tariffs are published separately and not yet read. The 1,376 toll plazas the RNC records are drawn as points, without fares.
No per-route length for the 國道 was found as open data, so a freeway's panel shows its measurement alone (D-63). The provincial highways have the Highway Bureau's register.

The Freeway Bureau publishes daily reference volumes per section without stating their unit or method, so a freeway's panel shows them by that name, as the busiest and the median section (D-64). The sections carry names and no coordinates, so a freeway's figures sit on its longest piece. The per-gantry ETC counts were not read; turning them into a per-route figure would be the atlas's own estimate.

The Highway Bureau's survey covers every provincial highway; its county-road stations are left out, as the atlas draws no county roads. Some stations record a survey weekday or a dated closure, which suggests counts on given days rather than a year-round average (D-65). 5 of 770 stations are not placed: 4 lie more than 5 km from their route, 1 is on 台61支線, which the atlas does not carry.

A provincial highway is drawn as its centrelines are. Where they leave a stretch out, it is a gap against the register's length: 台8 measures 161 km against 187.8, 台20 143 against 203.9, 台26 68 against 93.5, each across mountain or coast that has a gap of 14 km or more in the file. Why each stretch is absent, whether closed, unbuilt or unmapped, has not been traced.
The Taichung ring measures 23 km against the register's 37.8; the stitcher does not close it.
The Transport Department publishes no per-route length for Routes 1 to 10 in a form the atlas reads.

The Transport Department's Annual Traffic Census gives per-station AADT only in PDF appendices. Its ATC web viewer answers one station at a time from an undocumented interface, names stations by street rather than by route number, and states no licence; there is no census dataset on DATA.GOV.HK. It fails three tests of [DATA-SOURCES §2](DATA-SOURCES.md#2-what-a-source-must-meet): bulk machine-readable, joinable by designation, licence known.
The road network records no road class, so a route's freeway share is not given (D-63).

No Chinese authority publishes road geometry that can be read from abroad: Tianditu refuses foreign requests. The mainland is drawn from OpenStreetMap (D-66), which no authority stands behind. Its completeness varies by province, and a missing stretch, a wrong number or a road tagged with an old number is the mappers' and not the atlas's to correct.

The Ministry of Transport publishes network totals in its statistical bulletin, not per-route lengths or counts. A main route shows the plan's length as Chinese Wikipedia lists it, beside its measurement (D-72); link routes and provincial roads have their measurement alone, and no mainland route has traffic.
OpenStreetMap's toll tag covers too little of the expressway network to measure (D-69), so no mainland route has one.
How many provincial roads carry a number depends on how thoroughly each province is mapped. A number is each province's own (D-67), so S1 in Hebei and S1 in Sichuan are separate routes.
An end is named by the nearest mapped city or town, up to 120 km away in the west (D-68), not by the plan's terminus; the plan's ends are quoted beside, as the route relation tags them.

The American network is TIGER's primary and secondary roads. State systems TIGER files only among local roads are not drawn: North Carolina's secondary routes, South Carolina's S-roads, most Texas farm-to-market roads, and the like (D-47).

A freeway TIGER names without a number is titled by its name. Some states keep unsigned internal numbers for such roads (Kentucky's parkways are 9000-series); no source the atlas reads carries them, so none is shown (D-49).

TIGER 2025 does not yet carry the newest sections of I-295 around Fayetteville, so it is drawn at 14 of the Route Log's 22.48 mi. The headline shows FHWA's figure; the map is short until TIGER adds them.
Provincial routes the national file does not number

Alberta 12A and 834A, Nova Scotia 32, 33, 253, 280, 318, 322 and 328, and New Brunswick 151, 189, 194, 195 and 197 are in provincial registers or counts but carry no number in the National Road Network, so they are not drawn (D-50).
Traffic in BC, SK, MB, NL, YT, NU

The *Canada Year Book* (1951–1968, 1973) never reported Trans-Canada completion by province. Saskatchewan (21 August 1957) is the one exception. The only other dated event is the national opening on 3 September 1962, which was not a completion. The 1969–1972 editions, which would cover the programme's end, are missing from Statistics Canada's digitised collection. The Act, its amendments and each province's agreement date are on the timeline. Ontario's bridge years are drawn in the bridge layer as facts about bridges only.
Nova Scotia counts on unnumbered roads

103 of the 111 highways Nova Scotia counts attach to a route. The other eight cover 77 of 6,800 counted km, and they run on roads the National Road Network gives no route number: Hammonds Plains Rd (213), Purcells Cove Rd (253), and two Halifax arterials the province counts as 32 and 33. The province's own section geometry matches its counts but cannot supply a route the national file lacks.

CBSA's directory gives each of its 116 highway border offices an address and no coordinates. 97 are placed by the NRCan geocoder: 41 to an address, 33 to an intersection, 11 to a street and 12 to a place name only. 17 had no match near the border and are placed where the highway in their address meets the line. Beaver Creek (address a PO box) and Fraser (on BC 2, which the atlas draws only near Dawson Creek) are not placed. Of the 58 that pair with a US port in BTS's data, all but Piney lie within 25 km of it. Piney is 39 km from Pinecreek MN, though 2.9 km from the line.

Canada publishes none. The seven shown are 407 ETR, the Confederation Bridge, Cobequid Pass and the four international bridges of the Federal Bridge Corporation, each assembled from the documents that govern it. They are not every toll in the country.

A fare is shown only with the date it took effect, or the date since which the publisher says it has not changed. The Blue Water Bridge publishes its rates with neither, so none is shown, and no 407 ETR fare was recorded with one.

The three toll stretches are drawn along the atlas route between the ends the NRCan geocoder gives, and each is drawn only if that stretch is within 10% of the published length: 407 ETR measures 104.2 km against 108, the Confederation Bridge 13.7 against 12.9, Cobequid Pass 43.3 against 45. The four international bridges are points at their crossing or route end.
Which road a crossing is on
Neither register says. A crossing lists the atlas routes within 2 km of it, by distance alone; 149 of the 167 have one.

美国路网为 TIGER 的主要与次要道路（MTFCC S1100 与 S1200），其上的所有挂牌路线都包括在内。TIGER 只归入地方道路的州道不在范围内：北卡罗来纳的次要路线、南卡罗来纳的 S 字头道路、得克萨斯的大部分农场到市场道路。
HPMS 列出约 11,000 个本站没有的州道编号，几乎都是这类地方等级系统。为此读取 TIGER 全量道路文件被否决：它们相当于全国每一条街道，而乡间道路不是本站要画的东西。
名称本身就是编号的，即使 TIGER 标为 `M` 也按编号读取：波多黎各以「PR」或「Carr」开头的名称、任何地方以「I-」开头的名称，以及得克萨斯的 loop 和 spur，包括没写「State」的（泰勒的 Loop 49、圣安吉洛的 Loop 250）。TIGER 的表按 UTF-8 读取。
其他地方 `M` 表示俗名并被排除，但 TIGER 把波多黎各所有 carretera 都标为 `M`，包括 PR-52，因此整个岛都缺失了，拉雷多的「I-69 W」和这两条得克萨斯 loop 也一样。按 Windows-1252 读取时，「Peña Blvd」会变成「PeÃ±a」。
有名称无编号的 TIGER 主要道路，若 0.4 公里内没有编号路线，就并入某条路线。FHWA 路线名录显示该路是挂牌路线时，并入那条路线（Natcher Parkway 即 I-165）；否则自成一条路线，以名称为题，路牌留空，并注明没有编号，前提是长度达到 1 英里；更短的仍作背景线。不挂牌的内部编号（肯塔基的 9000 系列、新泽西的 444 和 700、俄克拉何马的收费公路编号）不显示。

S1100 是 TIGER 的限制出入等级，这些高速公路此前只画成背景细线：肯塔基的各条 parkway、John Kilpatrick 收费公路、波多黎各的快速路。更短的是普通干道上的立交（Jamboree Road、Cedar Avenue），不是高速公路。本站读取的来源都没有这些内部编号：HPMS 没有肯塔基 900x 或新泽西 444/700 的记录，它的俄克拉何马 375 长 209 英里，范围不同。
能证明登记错位的路线名录数字，用 `fhwa-corrections.json` 替换，每条都附 FHWA 公布的原值；公布值一旦变化，构建即失败。无法找回正确值的数字予以撤下，该路线改用实测值（D-1）。第一例是田纳西：两张表里该州的里程列从 I-69 到 I-840 整体错了一行。
错位后的数值逐条吻合：I-640 公布 77.29 英里（即 I-840 的长度），实测 11；I-81 公布 1.96（I-124 的），实测 76；I-75 公布 75.63（I-81 的），实测 159，等于 142.23 加上与 I-40 共线的 19.60 英里。只剔除明显不合理的行被否决，因为那样会留下看似合理却错误的数字。

TIGER 中名称登记有误的路段，按 `tiger-renames.json` 改读为正确名称；每条规则以 LINEARID 列出所涉路段并写明理由。TIGER 年份变化或某条规则不再匹配时，构建即失败。TIGER 沿同一条路画出去又折回来的线，若回程有 80% 位于去程 100 米以内，在最远端切开。走廊内的断点也从每段的两个地理端点出发跨接（D-56），因为 I-35 现在止于双城分岔处，而那里是两条车道汇合的节点。

双城分岔与合流之间只写 "I- 35" 的路段，逐段属于 I-35E 或 I-35W；M 类的 "Joe N Martin Expy" 就是 I-555；印第安纳州 265 号州道自 2019 年起为 I-265；I-11 自 2024 年起沿 US 95 从 Railroad Pass 到 Kyle Canyon；I-515 已撤销，路线名录中没有，予以去掉。一条折返线曾使 I-73 只量得 70 英里，其余画成分支。只按名称匹配被否决，因为分岔两侧的干线也叫 "I- 35"。凡两端相近就切开的做法被否决：环线也是这样画的，在 Fort Johnson 把一条环线切成两半，曾使 NY 5 的终点从奥尔巴尼移到 Tribes Hill。
`tiger.mjs` 中的 `loadRenames`、`unfold`；`build-data.mjs` 中的走廊拼接

blocks.text: 加拿大

head: 编号
决策
理由与被否决的方案
执行位置
rows: 保留 NRN 中的市县编号，该等级命名为「省道与市县道」，每条路以地名区分。
文件不区分二者；靠猜会丢掉真正的省道。
`RTNUMBER` 为 0 表示无编号；小数（`1.0`）去掉小数部分；纽芬兰的地方连接编号（`430-15`）排除。
每一种都曾产生假路线：一条 42,465 公里的「0 号公路」、2,504 条假的纽芬兰路线。
已由 D-52 取代。横加公路等级曾根据 NRN 的路段名称测定：承载它至少 25 公里且占全长 35% 的路线。
BC 的黄头公路和整个魁北克都没有这个名称，因此都被画成普通路线；而达到门槛的路线又被整条画成横加公路：400 号公路和 11 号公路全线。

横加公路是手工清单（`tch-routes.json`）上的路线：维基百科列出的主线与全部分支，十个省共 33 条。每条路线在横加公路终止处切开，只有承载它的那段画成横加公路，其余部分留在原来的等级。范围以省份记录的 NRN 路段名称为准，否则为整条路线（BC 1，其温哥华岛路段 NRN 未命名；BC 16、QC 85、QC 185）或两个立交之间的路段（ON 11，以免把 71 号公路以西一小段零散的命名路段画进去；以及 QC 40、25、20、117 和 15）。不在清单上的路线若带这个名称，是与清单路线共线的路面，忽略不计；`tch-crosscheck.json` 列出两类情况。渡轮航段不绘制。
该系统没有机读登记，因此作为小而封闭的集合，按[第 2 节](#2-what-a-source-must-meet)手工整理；加拿大交通部的背景介绍确认了主线和黄头公路，但没有列出分支，所以用百科全书来列举，这一点违背了权威性规则。只靠名称测定等级（D-21）因留下的缺口而被否决。
在安大略，横加公路路段以外，同一编号的各段只跨越 15 公里以内的断点相连；相距更远的各段作为同号的不同路线，以端点所在地区分；编号按长度排序，所以 `on-12-on-1` 是休伦县的县道，省道本身是 `on-12-on-3`。
安大略把县道登记在省道的编号下，所以 NHS 拼接（每处断点最多 120 公里）把 12 号公路惠特比–米德兰走廊和全省各地的 12 号县道连在一起，端点落在 350 公里外的埃塞克斯镇。省道路段只在穿城的连接段（connecting link）处断开，15 公里足以跨过。按道路等级区分省道和县道被否决，因为连接段和县道一样被归为干道（arterial）。
NHS 等级从加拿大交通部的服务读取。
加拿大统计局自己的 NHS 图层在西北地区和育空是空的。
交通量只从批量发布的辖区读取；每个数字是长度加权平均，并与最繁忙点并列显示。
地图和 PDF 不符合[第 2 节](#2-what-a-source-must-meet)；只给平均值会掩盖峰值。
安大略的共线路面计量方式按原样保留；新斯科舍的单向计数相加为双向数字；407 号公路运营方的出行次数不作为交通量显示。
每一条都在路线面板上说明。
通车年份只取自魁北克的名录和《年鉴》中注明日期的事件。
其他省份都没有公布；桥梁年份被拒绝（D-36）。

NRN 没有给编号的省道不收录，也不从其他来源补入。已知案例：艾伯塔 12A 和 834A；新斯科舍 32、33、253、280、318、322 和 328；新不伦瑞克 151、189、194、195 和 197；安大略十条 7000 系列连接线（7087 至 7908）和 7187；NHS 登记中的萨斯喀彻温 10A、育空 97 和魁北克 720。每一条都列在 `coverage-gaps.json` 中。
省级统计和登记里有它们，但只有 NRN 以符合[第 2 节](#2-what-a-source-must-meet)的许可提供加拿大的几何；省级统计文件的路段无法提供国家文件没有的道路。

head: 编号
决策
理由与被否决的方案
执行位置
rows: 路线编号以 INEGI 的 CODIGO 为准；SICT 的编号只做交叉核对，不合并。
两个机构各自为州道编号；合并会凭空造出路线。
只有有编号的道路才成为路线；2 公里以上的无编号联邦和州道作为淡色背景。
无编号的道路没有任何可以关联的编号。
MEX-15 与 MEX-15D 视为同一条路线；收费比例取自逐段标记。
文件几乎从不写 D 后缀。
联邦路段所在的州按 Natural Earth 1:10m 确定。
文件把每个联邦路段的管辖方都记为联邦。
路线端点为其所在的 SICT 路段（tramo）。
墨西哥数据流程中没有地名库。
`VELOCIDAD` 保留为 `routingSpeed`，从不作为限速显示。
它是路径规划参数，不是标示限速。
年平均日交通量按路线显示观测站数量及其中位数、最低和最高值；不做长度加权平均。位于无编号道路或距其路线超过 5 公里的观测站不放置。SICT 为 2024 年推算的 2,206 个站点会加以说明，因为数据本身没有标记。
观测站是点；按长度加权会凭空制造覆盖。
SICT 最新版中某州的行数不到上一年一半时，该州观测站改用十二年面板中上一年的数据。每个观测站带有年份，观测站跨两年的路线显示「2023–2024」。键为 `MEX-015D` 的观测站放在 MEX-015 上，因为 D-28 把二者视为同一路线。
2024 版在十二个州止于 99 行，两个资源都是如此（哈利斯科 99 行，2023 年为 734 行），这是截断而不是调查规模变小。全部改用 2023 年被否决，因为会丢掉完整的 2024 年州份。不做 D 后缀合并时，收费高速公路上有 2,000 多个观测站被丢弃。
只以 ramal、acceso 或偏移段命名的州道，若 SICT 2025 年索引在同一州为同名路段列出了同一编号，则保留。RNC 没有的 SICT 州道编号不放置。
一概排除这类路线（D-27 的理由，`isBranchOnly`）也会丢掉两个机构认定一致的道路：伊达尔戈的 HGO-017 Tepeji del Río–Tlahuelilpan、金塔纳罗奥的 QR-018。本站缺少的 122 个 SICT 州道编号中，大多是 RNC 编号不同（D-26）或按名称在其中找不到的道路；按位置放置它们被否决。
没有任何路段落在某州概化边界内的联邦路线，归入最近的州；其分州里程留空。
`mex-174`（华雷斯城）和 MEX-15 在索诺拉的一段曾被归入「MX」。把它们的路段塞进最近州的里程被否决，因为 D-29 让这类路段不归属任何州。
墨西哥路线的断点，除从死端出发外，也从每一段的两个地理端点出发跨接。只写在路段名称里的联邦编号不予读取。

RNC 把分隔的联邦公路画成两条单向车道，它们在每段的端点汇合，因此那里没有死端，剩下的跨接只能从匝道残段出发：MEX-85 从曼特到维多利亚跳过 117 公里，而它自己的一段 119 公里路就在两端 3 公里外，被画成分支，不计入长度。这些段断在另一编号的 CODIGO 接管共线路段之处（曼特的 MEX-80、新拉雷多的 MEX-2），因为该字段只能写一个编号。从 NOMBRE 读编号被否决：名称中写着联邦编号的路段共约 1,100 公里，几乎都是以所岔出的交叉口命名的州道（"E.C. México 15 – Ocoroni"），少数确实是该公路本身的是城市街道。

head: 编号
决策
理由与被否决的方案
执行位置
rows: 台湾的一条路线，就是 ROADNUM 写着该编号的全部国土测绘中心路段：國3甲即國道 3A，台14乙即省道 14B，天干甲至庚读作 A 至 G。临时编号（如台16臨29）不计入，共 209 段。快速公路台61 至台88 属于省道，与其他省道一同绘制。
编号就在来源里，无需匹配。临时线是原路线改建期间借用其编号的临时道路，画出来会让该路线重复。
台湾中心线使用 TWD97 TM2（EPSG:3826），用 Krüger 级数换算为经纬度，不引入投影库。
只有一个分带、一个公式，为此加依赖不划算。结果已用國1 基隆端核对。
台湾与香港路线的端点，写作端点所在道路在来源中的名称。公路局的起迄点与经过地名并列引用，不与端点对应。
两份文件都没有地名库。路线表写「臺北—楓港」，但没说画出的线哪一端是哪一个，按位置对应就是 D-2 拒绝的空间匹配。
省道的官方里程取自路线表，对照本站所画最长的一段；國道没有官方里程。香港道路网不记录道路等级，所以不给出其路线的高速公路比例。
没有在 data.gov.tw 或高速公路局的开放数据中找到逐条國道里程；是否改用其他出版物待定（[ACCURACY.md 第 6 节](ACCURACY.md#6-known-gaps)）。把香港每条干线都算作高速公路属于推断。
國道交通量采用高速公路局的日交通量参考值，并以此名称显示：平日最繁忙的主线路段，以及平日、周六、周日的路段中位数，两个方向相加。同一路段的两个方向按无序的起迄名称配对；没有配对的路段不计入。高架车道另列一行。数值放在该编号最长的一段上。
高公局没有说明单位和推算方法，称其为年平均日交通量就是说了来源没说的话。路段只有名称没有坐标，放在最长一段是唯一不靠猜测的做法。把國1 高架加到平面道路上会把同一走廊算两次。
省道交通量采用公路局的调查：每个测站两个方向相加，放到 5 km 内同编号最近的一段上，并按各测站代表的路段长度加权平均到整条路线，同时给出最繁忙测站、重型车与机车比例，以及测站覆盖的路线比例。面板会说明部分测站注明了调查日或某日的封路。东区分局的文件在测站名称处写的是工程处，因此这些测站以其路段起迄命名。
每个测站都写明它代表的路段，所以与墨西哥的点位（D-32）不同，长度加权来自来源本身。2025 年文件中 1,539 行有 442 行在「備註」注明星期（四、日、六），少数注明某日的封路，说明计数可能来自特定日期而非连续观测；公路局没有说明。

blocks.text: 中国大陆

head: 编号
决策
理由与被否决的方案
执行位置
rows: 中国大陆的线形取自 OpenStreetMap，这是[第 2 节](#2-what-a-source-must-meet)权威性要求的唯一例外。每条大陆路线的面板、标题长度下方与「关于」页都写明这一点；`data/geo/cn/` 下的数据是受 ODbL 约束的派生数据库。
官方的开放版本，即 1:100 万公众版全国基础地图，只通过天地图提供，而天地图对境外请求返回 HTTP 418；过去提供它的 webmap.cn 已不再提供。没有其他机构批量发布全国或省级道路几何。另一个选择是不画大陆；取自 OSM 并写明来源，让读者自己判断。商业地图服务直接否决：其条款禁止提取数据。

大陆路线是 `track` 及以上等级、在自身 `ref` 上或经 `route=road` 关系带有该编号的全部道路，按 GB/T 917 的写法读取：G 加一、二或四位数字，或两位数字加字母后缀，为国家高速公路；G 加三位数字为普通国道；S 为省道，每个使用该编号的省各算一条路线。标有「旧」「old」「原」的编号，以及 G0xx（被 2009 年标准取代的高速编号）不计入。县道（X）、乡道（Y）、村道（C）不读取。
编号就在来源里，无需匹配。省道编号由各省自定，把各省的 S1 归为一条路线会连起毫不相干的道路。县道由各县编号、数量多得多，与安大略的县道（D-50）一样会淹没省道层。
大陆道路按其中点所在的省归属，依据 Natural Earth 边界；概化海岸线漏掉的，取 0.2° 内最近的省；两者都不在的，位于大陆以外，不计入。路线端点以 OSM 中 30 km 内最近的城市或镇命名，城市优先于近 8 km 以内的镇；没有则放宽到 120 km，并显示距离。
提取范围越过国界，延伸到蒙古、缅甸、香港与澳门。青藏高原和塔克拉玛干的大部分路线端点 30 km 内没有城镇，未命名的端点不如带距离的命名端点提供的信息多。
大陆的 motorway 无论是否标有 `toll=yes` 都算作高速公路，大陆路线一律不给收费比例。
该标签覆盖不到高速网的三分之一：长于 50 英里的 223 条高速中只有 70 条有一半以上长度带此标签，而这个路网几乎全程收费。由它得出的比例衡量的是制图而不是道路。
国道与国家高速的名称与规划起讫，取描述整条路线的那个路线关系（先看全称，再看是否两端齐全，再看名称是否不带路段或方向限定），并去掉「（四川段）」「（北京方向）」之类的限定；起讫按原文引用，不与画出的线对应。
贡献者把一条路线的关系按省或按方向拆开，每段都重复路线名称并加上自己的限定，因此只取成员最多的一段，会让 G318 以其四川段命名。
国家级编号的各段跨越 30 km 以内的缺口拼接，再将拼好的各段跨越 80 km 以内拼接；省道跨越 15 km。某省道编号若另有更长的段，不足 2 km 的段舍去。
OSM 的编号道路在每个被贡献者切分却没带上 ref 的路口断开；断成几百段的国道不是读者能沿着看的路线。路口处的省道残段是标了编号的匝道，不是道路。

blocks.text: 三者从不混用、平均，也不互相填补。
长度、端点、分辖区里程、直线距离和道路等级构成，都由本站根据实测道路几何计算；几何为绘图做了抽稀，但没有重画。一条路线沿着从一端到另一端的唯一路径量取，因此分向行驶的公路只计一次，而不是每条车行道各计一次。凡 FHWA 名录有数字的，构建都会与之比较，并把差异分布写入 `data/stats.json`；README 从那里引用。

较大的差异大多可以解释，而不是错误，本站会解释它们，而不是取个折中。FHWA 把两条州际公路共用的路面只记在其中一条名下，因此 I-90 与 I-80 共用印第安纳收费公路的那段，在名录里算 I-80 的，在本站两条都算，这就是 I-90 比公布值长 13.7% 的原因。名录本身也有疏漏：它的田纳西一列错了一行，诺克斯维尔约 7 英里长的环路 I-640 因此得到了 I-840 的 77.29。这些数字由一份提交在库中的更正表替换，每条都保留公布原值（[D-53](DATA-SOURCES.md#5-decision-log)）。除此之外，两个数字始终都会显示，也都不会向对方靠拢。
算法以及它无法正确测量的情况，见 [ARCHITECTURE.md 第 3 节](ARCHITECTURE.md#3-from-fragments-to-routes)。
交通量、货车流量、路况、车道数、标示限速和道路最近一次改善的年份，是各州实测并上报给 FHWA 的数据，按编号关联到路线，从不按位置。覆盖程度本来就不均匀：路况在国家公路系统上调查得很全面，在其他地方则零零星星，因此这些数字每一个都注明它覆盖了路线的多大比例。
**加拿大没有对应的全国采集。**没有全国性的交通量统计，因为计数由各省负责，是否发布、以何种形式、按什么条款，都由各省自行决定。不发布的省份，其路线不显示交通量，而不是显示推算值。

blocks.text: 每个省级数字都是沿路线按长度加权的平均值，与该路最繁忙点的流量（如果两者不同）并列显示。401 号公路全线平均每天 73,700 辆车，但在 427 号公路与 Renforth Drive 之间每天通行 511,400 辆，是本站任何地方单点计数的最高值。安大略的 407 号公路是唯一显眼的空白：收费路段按 99 年特许经营运营，不在主管部门的计数之内，运营方公布的是工作日平均出行次数，那不是日交通量，也不会被当作日交通量显示。

**墨西哥按点计数。**SICT 的《道路数据》给出全国铺装路网上各观测站的年平均日交通量（TDPA，相当于 AADT）。路线显示统计了多少个观测站，以及它们的中位数、最低和最高值。不计算长度加权平均，因为观测站是点而不是路段，按长度加权会凭空制造 SICT 并未发布的覆盖。2024 版在十二个州止于 99 行，而 2023 年有几百行，因此这些州的观测站用的是 2023 年数据。每条路线都说明它显示的是哪一年，跨两类州的路线显示「2023–2024」。
州际公路官方里程来自 FHWA 路线名录与查找表；加拿大的编号认定和路网里程来自加拿大交通部。路线说明中的一切（造价、交通量、建设日期、路况）都附有自己的来源行，写明出版物及其日期。收费设施每条事实各附一个来源，费率只与其生效日期一同显示。

没有公布数字的地方，本站会直说，而不是估算。黄头公路由四个省历经数十年修建和延伸，没有任何部门公布过它的总造价，所以它的页面写明这一点，而不是编一个数字。`build-content.mjs` 强制执行这一规则：数字必须附来源或说明为何缺失，中英文都要有，否则构建失败。路线说明把造价记为未公开、而 FHWA 逐条路线造价表有数字时，构建会删除路线说明的这一说法并报告出来，因此页面永远不会在一个有来源的数字旁边印出「无公开数字」。
加拿大的国家道路文件把县级、市级路线编号和省道编号记在同一个字段里，没有任何区分标记：安大略有二十二条互不相干的道路都编号为 21。它们全部照原样发布，而不是靠猜测筛选；等级名称也据此命名，每条路都附上能识别它的地名。
TIGER 给每段道路只起一个名字。两条路线共用路面时，这段路只带一个编号，另一条路线在这里就出现缺口。路是画出来了，用的是另一个编号，但失去标签的那条路线量得偏短：有几条州际公路仅因此就低于 FHWA 的里程。凡有 FHWA 数字的，路线页面都会把它与实测值并列显示。
授予日期不是通车日期。SICT 的特许经营登记记录的是证书何时授予；对于修建道路的证书，本站把这个日期显示为道路最早可能通车的日期，并加以说明。
「来源」表示没有发布者以可用形式发布；「待做」表示数据可得，尚未做出来。

省道有多少带编号，取决于各省地图的完整程度。编号由各省自定（D-67），河北的 S1 与四川的 S1 是两条路线。
端点以最近的已绘城市或镇命名，西部最远可达 120 km（D-68），而不是规划中的起讫点；规划起讫按路线关系的标签并列引用。
美国路网为 TIGER 的主要与次要道路。TIGER 只归入地方道路的州道系统不绘制：北卡罗来纳的次要路线、南卡罗来纳的 S 字头道路、得克萨斯的大部分农场到市场道路等（D-47）。
TIGER 只有名称没有编号的高速公路以名称为题。有些州为这类道路保留不挂牌的内部编号（肯塔基的 parkway 是 9000 系列）；本站读取的来源都没有这些编号，所以不显示（D-49）。

魁北克以外的通车年份
《加拿大年鉴》（1951–1968、1973）从未按省报告横加公路的完工情况。萨斯喀彻温（1957 年 8 月 21 日）是唯一的例外。另一个注明日期的事件是 1962 年 9 月 3 日的全国通车，那并不是完工。可能涵盖工程收尾的 1969–1972 年各版不在加拿大统计局的数字化馆藏中。该法案、其修正案以及各省的协议日期都在时间线上。安大略的桥梁年份只作为关于桥梁的事实绘于桥梁图层。
新斯科舍在无编号道路上的计数
新斯科舍统计的 111 条公路中有 103 条关联到路线。其余八条覆盖 6,800 公里计数中的 77 公里，位于国家道路网没有给路线编号的道路上：Hammonds Plains Rd（213）、Purcells Cove Rd（253），以及该省按 32 和 33 统计的两条哈利法克斯干道。该省自己的路段几何与其计数一致，但无法提供国家文件没有的路线。

边境服务局名录给其 116 个公路边境办事处各一个地址，没有坐标。97 个由 NRCan 地理编码放置：41 个到门牌地址，33 个到交叉口，11 个到街道，12 个只到地名。17 个在边境附近没有匹配，放在其地址中的公路与边境线的交点。Beaver Creek（地址是邮政信箱）和 Fraser（位于 BC 2，本站只在道森克里克附近绘制它）未放置。在 BTS 数据中与美国口岸配对的 58 个里，除 Piney 外都在 25 公里以内。Piney 距明尼苏达州 Pinecreek 39 公里，但距边境线 2.9 公里。
加拿大没有发布。显示的七处是 407 ETR、联邦大桥、Cobequid Pass 以及联邦桥梁公司的四座国际桥梁，每一处都根据管理它的文件整理而成。它们不是全国所有的收费设施。
费率只与其生效日期，或发布者声明自该日起未变的日期一同显示。蓝水桥公布费率时两者都没有，因此不显示；407 ETR 的费率也都没有记录到日期。
三个收费段沿本站路线，在 NRCan 地理编码给出的两端之间绘制，且只有长度与公布值相差 10% 以内时才绘制：407 ETR 测得 104.2 公里，公布 108；联邦大桥 13.7，公布 12.9；Cobequid Pass 43.3，公布 45。四座国际桥梁是位于口岸或路线端点的点。
